extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent practitioners filing or prosecuting national (Finland) and PCT patent applications with PRH
extracted.subtask_description: Official PRH handbook guidance for preparing, filing, and prosecuting national patent and utility model applications (and related PCT handling) before the Finnish PRH, including procedural requirements, timelines, accelerated routes, language and document rules, fees, and post‑grant procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents (required parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application comprises the application form with annexes. The annexes must include the description of the invention, patent claims, any drawings, and an abstract; where applicable also a priority document, statement of right to the invention, and power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handbook treats the separate parts in detail (B.3–B.6). The application must be made in writing and the appearance/form of documents is subject to further rules (B.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter (statutory exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent may be granted for any technical invention that is industrially applicable, new, and essentially different from what was known before the filing date. Certain subject matter is not considered a technical invention and is excluded from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of exclusions listed: mere discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods, artistic creations, rules/plans/methods for intellectual activity/game/business, computer programs, presentation of information, and surgical/therapeutic/diagnostic methods directed to humans or animals (PatL §§ referenced). See E.6 and E.8.1.1 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of filing and decision language
rubrics_metrics.description: National patent applications may be filed in Finnish, Swedish or English; the language of the application determines the language used in PRH proceedings. PCT applications to be received by PRH must be in Finnish, Swedish or English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed in English and English prosecution is requested, PRH will prepare decisions in English up to grant; post‑grant phases (e.g., oppositions, SPC) require Finnish or Swedish. Utility model applications must be in Finnish or Swedish; foreign applicants must file utility model applications in Finnish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document submission channels and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents may be submitted to PRH electronically (24/7) or on paper. Electronic filings via Patenttiasiointi service or browser-based application are supported; priority documents may be submitted via WIPO DAS; ePCT may be used for PCT filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email submissions are accepted only if attachments can be opened by PRH. Paper documents must be white A4 or equivalent electronic formats; the application number must appear on the first page of any correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities check before substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Every application undergoes a formal (formalities) examination. Only when formal requirements are satisfied does the application proceed to technical examination (search and patentability assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formal defects exist, PRH issues a substantiated interim decision (välipäätös) setting a deadline to correct them. Multiple formal objections may remove an application from accelerated processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and substantive patentability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: In technical examination PRH performs a novelty search and evaluates patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability) to form its technical interim decisions and final decision on grant or refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PCT national phase, international search (ISA) and optional international preliminary examination (IPEA) steps are described separately in Part K. ITS and ITS-like searches are also available on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of PRH decisions and written communication rule
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH issues decisions, interim decisions, and communications in writing. PRH does not notify decisions by ordinary email; decisions are transmitted via the document service or by post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal contact (phone, remote meetings) can be used to expedite processes or clarify technical terms, but no decisions are made orally. Any relevant informal discussion is documented in the file and the applicant may submit a written response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a patent attorney (representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may be represented by a patent attorney. Use of a patent attorney is recommended (especially for drafting claims and prosecution) but not mandatory for domestic applicants; foreign applicants without domicile in Finland must have an EEA‑resident representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent attorneys help evaluate patentability pre-filing, draft claims to provide business‑appropriate protection, and manage prosecution. PRH maintains a register of authorized patent attorneys via the industrial property attorney board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and response times (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim decisions will specify deadlines by which the applicant must respond or correct defects. Statutory deadlines for national matters are at least two months unless otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a deadline falls on a PRH holiday/closure the document can be filed the next open day. Specific rules for patent vs utility model deadlines are in the patent and utility model regulations; SPC matters often have three‑month response times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time (request and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH may extend statutory deadlines on its own initiative or upon applicant request. The applicant must request extensions in writing before the given deadline expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting up to two months extension and it is the first extension in the application processing, no justification is required. Further extensions require detailed justification and are granted only for special reasons. Requesting an extension ends accelerated processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-establishment of rights (oikeuden ennalleen palauttaminen)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant or proprietor has lost a right because of failure to perform a required act within a deadline, the rights may be restored under specified conditions (PatL 71a §, HmL 26a §).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handbook references further details in chapter C.7 on the required conditions and procedures for re‑establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRH processing time targets
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH aims to issue the first technical interim decision within eight months of filing and to complete national patent prosecution within three years where possible. Utility model average processing time is about two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well‑drafted applications and prompt responses to interim decisions accelerate the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated processing at filing (national accelerated procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request accelerated processing at the time of filing. PRH will aim to perform a search and issue the first technical interim within three months of transfer to technical examination and the second interim within two months of the applicant's response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The accelerated request must be filed the same day as the application and be justified. Eligibility requires the work situation in the technical field to permit fast examination and that the application meets one of: (1) concerns bioeconomy/circular economy/clean tech, (2) applicant intends to pursue PPH, or (3) applicant provides a significant economic or other compelling reason. No fee is charged. Formality objections can remove the application from accelerated processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) usage and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH is an inter‑office cooperation route to obtain accelerated examination based on favorable findings in a partner office. PRH will accelerate processing to final disposition when presented with an acceptable PPH request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be substantively corresponding between offices. PPH requests are filed directly to the office whose examination is to be accelerated. Offices have varying PPH requirements, so applicants should consult partner office guidance. Filing a PPH request to PRH is free.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) handling at PRH as Receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH may act as the Receiving Office for PCT filings (in Finnish, Swedish, or English). PRH performs initial formalities checks before the application proceeds to the international authority for search and optional preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PCT process includes an ISA international search and an optional IPEA international preliminary examination. PRH can act as an ISA/IPEA in certain circumstances; PCT phases are described in Part K.

rubrics_metrics.name: International‑type search (ITS) on national application
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request an international‑type search (ITS) for a national patent application (PatL 9 §); PRH aims to complete ITS within 4–5 months of request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ITS report is provided to the national examiner and the national application is then processed forward promptly upon receipt of the search report. ITS processing details are in chapter K.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity and confidentiality of application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application documents become public either on grant (national patent) or 18 months from the filing or earliest priority date. Utility model documents become public upon registration or by 15 months from filing/priority date. Prior to public availability the files are confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH publishes documents for public patents, utility models and SPCs. The patent system is based on exchange: a time‑limited monopoly in exchange for public disclosure of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees, duration and renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: A pending application or a granted patent is maintained by payment of annual fees. Patents can be maintained up to 20 years from filing. Utility model registration initially lasts four years and can be renewed twice (first for four years, then two years) up to a maximum of 10 years from filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPC (supplementary protection certificate) extends protection under specified EU regulations and requires a separate application. Details and current fee schedules are available on PRH's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Final PRH decisions in national patent and utility model matters may be appealed to the Market Court; further appeal to the Supreme Administrative Court is possible only with leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals to the Market Court must be filed within 60 days of notification and require payment of a fee. Further appeal to the highest court (KHO) must be filed within 30 days of the Market Court decision and requires leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑grant opposition (väite) at PRH
rubrics_metrics.description: After grant and the nine‑month opposition (väite) period, third parties may file a väite against the granted patent to request its cancellation; PRH handles such oppositions during the nine‑month period following grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the nine‑month period has lapsed, the only way to annul a national patent is via court (mitätöintikanne) in the Market Court. PRH also outlines procedures for opposition handling in chapter G.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement enforcement is private (patent holder responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement against infringement is the responsibility of the patent proprietor; if infringement occurs and parties cannot agree, the proprietor must initiate litigation (loukkauskanteet) in Market Court or, for unitary/EP/UPC matters, in the relevant forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH does not conduct infringement proceedings; it only grants and administers rights. For unitary patents and UPC jurisdiction, UPC handles all related litigation per the applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and technical requirements for communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents submitted to PRH (letters and attachments) must be in formats accessible to PRH and comply with page/format requirements (white A4 paper or equivalent electronic document). Application number should be indicated on first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submission recommendations include use of Patenttiasiointi; PRH will not rely on personal email addresses of employees and prescribes official channels on its website for submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of formal objections on accelerated procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If PRH issues a formal interim decision for defects before the search (or issues multiple formal objections), the application may be removed from accelerated processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in accelerated streams must correct formal defects within the set deadline; failure or subsequent formal objections ends accelerated handling and the application proceeds on the normal timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum statutory timeframe references and regulatory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural deadlines and minimum response times are governed by national patent statutes and regulations (PatL, PatA, PatM) and corresponding utility model law and regulations; PRH follows these legal provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: minimum statutory deadline generally at least two months per patent/utility model regulations; PCT timelines (ISA reports within 3 months or 9 months from priority depending on rule 45.1; IPEA reports by 28 months per PCT rules). Applicants should consult Finlex and PRH references for current statutory provisions.
